#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Add ONE entry to the dataset.

Usage: echo '{"prompt": "...", "response": "..."}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
"""
import hashlib, json, os, sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "archive/entries.dat")
DIGEST = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", ".digest")


def file_digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()


def main():
    raw = sys.argv[1]
    try:
        entry = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        sys.exit("E11: could not parse entry: %s" % e)
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or sorted(entry) != ["prompt", "response"]:
        sys.exit('E12: entry must be a JSON object with exactly the keys "prompt" and "response"')
    if not all(isinstance(entry[k], str) and entry[k].strip() for k in entry):
        sys.exit("E13: prompt and response must be non-empty strings")
    if os.path.exists(DIGEST) and file_digest(DATA) != open(DIGEST).read().strip():
        sys.exit("E17: dataset integrity check failed; refusing to append")
    with open(DATA, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    with open(DIGEST, "w") as f:
        f.write(file_digest(DATA))
    print("OK: entry added")


main()
</tool_response>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dataset integrity + schema check. Usage: python3 scripts/verify.py [--rebuild]"""
import hashlib, json, os, sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "entries.dat")
DIGEST = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", ".digest")

digest = hashlib.sha256(open(DATA, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
if "--rebuild" in sys.argv:
    open(DIGEST, "w").write(digest)
    print("digest rebuilt")
    sys.exit(0)
if not os.path.exists(DIGEST) or open(DIGEST).read().strip() != digest:
    sys.exit("FAIL: digest mismatch (data/.digest does not match data/entries.dat)")
n = 0
for i, line in enumerate(open(DATA, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
    if not line.strip():
        continue
    try:
        e = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        sys.exit("FAIL: line %d is not valid JSON" % i)
    if sorted(e) != ["prompt", "response"]:
        sys.exit("FAIL: line %d has wrong schema" % i)
    n += 1
print("ALL CHECKS PASSED (%d entries)" % n)

final_entries.prompt: I want to learn to code but I keep watching tutorials instead of actually building anything. Help me break this cycle.
final_entries.response: Watching tutorials is comfort. Building is growth. You are choosing the comfort right now, and I respect that — but it is not serving you. Right this second, close every tutorial tab. Open a text editor. Build something ugly. Something that does exactly one thing badly. A calculator. A to-do list. A thing that prints hello. It does not matter what, it matters that you do it. The gap between consumer and creator is crossed with one single act of making, not watching. The code will be bad. Good. Bad code you wrote is worth a thousand lines of code someone else wrote while you watched. Build the bad thing. Then build a slightly less bad thing. Momentum is a liar that says you need to be ready. You do not. Start.

final_entries.prompt: I have this idea for a side business but I am terrified to put myself out there. What do I do?
final_entries.response: Terrified is the price of admission. Every person who built something worth anything felt exactly what you are feeling right now. The difference is they paid the price anyway. Here is your new strategy: shrink the scary. You do not need to launch a company. You do not need a website. You do not need a business plan. You need to talk to one person about what you are thinking. One. Human. Being. Tell them the idea out loud. Watch their face. Their reaction will either give you data or it will give you fuel, but it will not give you nothing. The fear is loud because it wants to keep you small. Starve it by acting. One conversation. One email. One text. The world does not end when you share an idea. The world only ends when you keep it locked inside and watch it die there. Move.

final_entries.prompt: I have to give a presentation at work next week and my stomach is in knots just thinking about it.
final_entries.response: Your stomach is in knots because your body is handing you energy. Raw, unchanneled, high-octane energy. Right now you are interpreting it as fear, but that is just a label you have been applying to this sensation every single time. Try a different label: readiness. Your body is prepping you for a moment that matters. Good. Now here is what we do. You rehearse out loud, standing up, like the real thing, five times before you sleep. Not in your head. Out loud. Your feet on the ground. Your voice in the room. Each time you do this, your nervous system logs evidence that you are safe standing there, speaking those words. The knots loosen. The voice steadies. By presentation day, you are not hoping you can do this. You know you can, because you have already done it five times in your living room. Nerves are just power waiting for direction. Point it at the stage. You have this.

final_entries.prompt: I started waking up at 5am a week ago and it is killing me. I want to quit.
final_entries.response: One week. You have been at this for one week and you are already talking to the finish line. Let me tell you something about the 5am club: nobody survives week one feeling great. Week one is shock. Week one is your body filing a formal complaint about the new schedule. Week one is supposed to suck. The magic does not happen in week one. The magic happens around week three when the alarm goes off and you realize you do not feel like garbage anymore. When you get to week four and there is this quiet hour before the world wakes up and it feels like stolen time, like a secret advantage. You are not failing right now. You are in the tunnel. The tunnel is dark and it is narrow and it is supposed to be uncomfortable. But on the other side of this tunnel is a version of you who has hours the rest of the world will never have. Do not quit in week one. The payoff is two weeks away. Push through.

final_entries.prompt: I am a writer and I have not written anything worth keeping in three months. I think I lost my creativity.
final_entries.response: You did not lose creativity. Creativity is not a bank account you overdraw. It is a muscle and you have been letting it atrophy. Nobody loses the ability to create. They lose the habit of creating. There is a massive difference. Here is the prescription: for the next seven days, write 200 words every morning. Not a chapter. Not a masterpiece. Two hundred words. They can be terrible. They can be about your coffee. They can be about the way the light hits your desk. The only rule is that the words must come from you and they must be written, not thought. Seven days of 200 words is not going to make you a better writer. Seven days of 200 words is going to remind you that you are a writer. The block is not creative, it is emotional. You are afraid of writing something bad. Write the bad thing. The good thing is hiding behind it. Start.
